chapter: Union career, Masons, mentoring and the Clef Club
title: Cleaning at the union and rising to financial secretary
summary: After leaving playing he took a union cleaning job, later became financial secretary, and went to school for accounting.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Always playing. Always playing. Every time you'd turn around you'd see me with a saxophone. And I don't know why. I tried my best to get myself straightened. And do you know what happened to me? Can I tell you this?
Sure.
Do you know what happened to me when I left and I stopped playing and I went to the Union?
What?
I took a job up there and I was -- at the union, cleaning up the place, you know, like that. And I didn't have to do it.
At Local 76?
Yeah.
Well, weren't you also financial secretary there?
(chuckle)
Yeah, after I got straightened out again.
But at first you were just cleaning up, and you weren't financial secretary, you just went there
Yeah.
And you finally moved into being financial secretary?
Yeah, I finally moved into being financial secretary.
So again, that background that you had. You had gone to school before that.
Oh, yeah, I went to school for it. Oh, I forgot to tell you that.
Uh-huh.
I went to the -- what's the name of that school, right up there close -- was at 8th Street, upstairs.
Uh-huh.
Oh, boy.
So you had to go to school, what, in the day or night, because you were still a working musician, weren't you?
Daytime.
Daytime, yeah. Studying to be what, an accountant?
Yeah, studying to be an accountant. Oh, boy. I can't remember all of this. I wish I could get some of it down here.
